---
title: "Threat and Obligation in British Legislative Discourse"
---

**Status:** Research project / proposed doctoral research (update to reflect your current status).

## Overview

This project examines how British parliamentary debates surrounding the Online Safety Act construct competing representations of digital threats, regulatory obligations, privacy, and free expression.

## Framework

- Corpus-Assisted Discourse Studies (CADS)
- Text World Theory (TWT)
- Socio-Cognitive Critical Discourse Analysis

## Research design

Planned analysis includes keyword and collocation patterns, concordance-based examination of modality, and qualitative interpretation of world-building and world-switching.

## Outputs

Publications, conference presentations, and supporting materials will be listed here when available.
